title: Service economics and deployment simplicity brief
content:
One‑pager: why Redwood matters to platforms, product leaders, and finance

Short thesis
Redwood turns inference from an unpredictable cost center into a measurable, controllable service — by making latency, capacity and spend first‑class controls across hosted, dedicated and private deployments. The competitive switch is from owning models to managing the economics and reliability of serving them.

Mission framing (1 line)
Make inference predictable: performance, cost, and compliance under a single operational model.

Three pillars (how we deliver the thesis)
1) Predictable unit economics
   - Measureable per‑token and per‑QPS cost insights at the token/routing level.
   - Autoscaling and dedicated pools to absorb peak traffic without surprise bills.
   - Cost controls: intelligent batching/cache recommendations and quantization profiles to optimize spend with bounded quality regressions.
2) Deployment equivalence
   - Same API, same rollout controls and observability whether hosted, dedicated or private (VPC/on‑prem).
   - Migration story: test on hosted, validate with dedicated, then lift into private with identical operational primitives.
   - Reduces platform lock and operational rework during growth phases.
3) Reliability as a product feature
   - SLO-driven routing with graceful fallback to cheaper/compatible model variants.
   - Token-level tracing, per-route dashboards and regression alerts tied to eval suites.
   - SLA-backed dedicated tiers and admin controls for enterprise security/compliance.

Topline positioning bullets (for 30s pitch)
- For engineering and platform teams: Redwood is the inference runtime that behaves like a service — you get predictable latency, well‑understood unit cost, and simple rollouts.
- For product and revenue owners: Redwood ensures you can scale features without sudden spikes in cost or regressions in quality.
- For procurement/CFO: Redwood offers capacity commitments, measurable usage units, and controls that turn inference from an unknown variable into a forecastable line item.

Proof points / evidence to cite in conversations
- Observability: token + route cost breakdowns that let teams find the 10% savings that matter.
- Workloads migrated: customers using hosted -> dedicated -> private with no change to API integrations.
- Cost reductions: typical recommendation-driven configs show 20–40% per-token cost improvement on generator workloads. (internal benchmark reference available on Confluence)

Competitive differentiation (short rebuttals)
- Against hosted-only APIs: They simplify access but leave you exposed to unpredictable spend and limited deployment options. Redwood gives hosted simplicity plus enterprise-grade predictability and evacuation options.
- Against self-hosted runtimes: They give control but force teams to absorb ops work. Redwood provides the same control surface, plus a battle‑tested runtime and ops tooling that significantly shortens time-to-stable-production.
- Against cloud vendor endpoints: Cloud endpoints can feel commoditized on price but not on latency variability and rollout tooling. Redwood optimizes for stable tail latency and rollout confidence.

Common customer objections + rebuttals
- "We can host models ourselves": True, but compare full TCO (ops, oncall, model upgrades, kernel tuning) vs. Redwood’s predictable capacity and hands-off upgrades. Offer a short cost/ops delta analysis.
- "Open models are free": Models aren’t the only cost. Serving, scaling, and QA are material. Redwood reduces those variable costs and the business risk from regressions.
- "Vendor lock concern": Redwood’s API and deployment parity are specifically designed to avoid lock — we encourage staged migrations and support exportable configs.

Suggested one‑slide outline for sales decks
- Headline: Predictable inference at product scale
- 3 bullets (Economics / Deployment parity / Reliability)
- Quick customer quote (platform eng or CFO)
- 2‑line ask: trial with hosted, dedicated evaluation, or private pilot

Short outreach language (email opener)
Hi [Name],
We help platform teams turn inference from a variable cost and operational headache into a predictable, SLA-backed service. Can we run a 30‑day pilot that shows token-level cost visibility and a proposed capacity plan for your peak traffic?

Next steps for GTM team
- Create a 2‑page datasheet focused on CFO + Platform leads with concrete cost comparison templates.
- Build a one-click hosted->dedicated checklist for solutions engineering.
- Add a reference pack: 2 customer case studies (cost & latency delta) and an ops runbook excerpt.

Open questions / hypotheses to validate in customer calls
- What is the percent variance in customers’ monthly inference spend today? (target: >25% variance = high priority message)
- Which procurement terms (commits, SLAs, data residency) unblock enterprise deals?
- Which internal personas actually own the billing SLOs vs the latency SLOs?

Notes to self
Keep iteration light — this doc is tactical for Q4 enablement. Wire the datasheet to the internal cost-benchmarks page and route the pilot signup flow into the Solutions Engineering queue.
